title: Iskender Kebab
subtitle: Turkish doner meat on flatbread with tomato sauce and yoghurt
excerpt: Thin slices of spiced lamb and beef layered over torn flatbread, covered in a sharp tomato sauce, a pool of yoghurt alongside, and hot butter poured over the top at the table. A Bursa classic.
sourceNotes: Originated in Bursa, Turkey in the 19th century, attributed to Iskender Efendi. The home version uses pan-cooked spiced meat in place of a rotating doner.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: The tomato sauce can be made up to 3 days ahead. Cook the meat fresh.

content.text: Iskender is an assembly dish: flatbread, spiced meat, tomato sauce, and yoghurt layered in order, then finished with hot butter poured over just before serving. The bread should absorb the sauce and butter rather than stay crisp. Watch the butter closely; it should foam and brown but not burn.
Mix both minces with the grated onion, garlic, sweet paprika, cumin, cinnamon, and salt. Knead together for 2 minutes until smooth and cohesive. Shape into a flat oval about 2cm thick.

Make the tomato sauce. Heat the olive oil in the saucepan over a medium heat. Add the tomato puree and stir for 1 minute. Add the tinned tomatoes and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thickened. Season with salt.
Heat the frying pan over a high heat. Cook the meat oval for 5 minutes per side until cooked through and well browned. Transfer to a board and slice thinly.
Warm the pitta pieces briefly in the same frying pan for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Divide the warm pitta pieces among four plates. Lay the meat slices on top. Spoon the tomato sauce generously over the meat and bread. Add a large spoonful of yoghurt beside each serving.
Melt the butter in a small pan over a medium heat until it foams and turns light brown. Stir in the paprika. Pour this immediately over the plated dishes and serve at once.

items.symptom: The meat is crumbly and falls apart when sliced.
items.cause: The mince was not kneaded long enough to bind.
items.fix: Knead for at least 2 minutes until the mixture is sticky and holds together when pressed.

items.symptom: The yoghurt curdles on the plate.
items.cause: Hot sauce poured directly onto cold yoghurt.
items.fix: Bring the yoghurt to room temperature before serving and pour the sauce beside rather than on top of it.

items.symptom: The bread is still dry and chewy.
items.cause: The sauce did not soak in.
items.fix: Let the assembled dish sit for 2 minutes before pouring the butter so the bread absorbs the tomato sauce first.
